These are uncalibrated MuJoCo demonstrations with custom controllers. They establish a runnable evaluation workflow. They do not establish flight readiness, fleet reliability, automatic bug diagnosis, or hardware validity.

What happened on held-out scenarios

40 scenarios per vehicle, each run on both controllers with the same exogenous noise seed. All runs were conclusive and exercised the loss-of-link policy. Failure means any declared recovery or safety rule was violated.

VehicleControllerViolationsFailure fraction95% Wilson interval

0 failures in 40 rover runs still leaves a 95% upper bound of 8.8% under this synthetic distribution. The guarded quadrotor still failed 27 of 40 cases. Its 5 improved pairs and 1 regressed pair do not establish statistical superiority.

Mission contracts
The source, tests, models and JSON contract were hashed before the campaign. Development included nominal, long-outage and severe combined cases. Held-out seeds were generated after this internal freeze; this is not third-party preregistration.
Recovery requires all target predicates to hold together for the complete closed-grid dwell window, completed by the deadline. A brief threshold crossing cannot pass. Missing telemetry remains inconclusive unless a known breach already establishes a violation.


Search and reduction
VehicleMethodSimulation budgetRecovery violations foundBest normalized robustness
One 12-attempt run per method per vehicle. These results do not establish a search-method advantage. Lower robustness means a stronger violation under the declared scales.
Reduction preserves a selected recovery violation across 3 predeclared noise seeds. Cost is an editorial normalized fault-severity score, not physical risk or reliability. Greedy reduction and leave-one-hook-out ablations identify scenario sensitivity; they do not locate an unknown code defect or generate a repair.


Reproducibility with negative controls
VehicleCheckObserved grade
Exact replay and full-state checkpoint continuation are demonstrated only for this recorded source/environment. Deliberate state perturbations diverged. Deliberate source mismatches were rejected as incompatible. Hashes are integrity checks, not signatures or a proof of model correctness.


What changed—and what remains
Implemented
  • MuJoCo rigid-body dynamics: wheel contact and a free six-DOF quadrotor with four rotor forces.
  • Lag, actuator limits, unequal authority, air-relative drag, wind and friction uncertainty.
  • Noisy delayed GNSS, stale source timestamps, outages/bias, IMU prediction and complementary correction.
  • Independent loss-of-link processing, stale/innovation guards and explicit degraded modes.
  • Finite-trace monitor plus separately implemented boolean oracle and analytic physics checks.
Open validation work
  • Fit plants, sensors and fault distributions to measured vehicle data.
  • Integrate an actual PX4/ArduPilot controller; neither is connected here.
  • Replace synthetic attitude aiding with a validated sensor/AHRS model.
  • Expand return, land and continue policies; only rover STOP and quadrotor HOLD are implemented.
  • Improve quadrotor control, validate on fresh held-out scenarios, then move to SITL/HIL and controlled physical testing.


Sources: MuJoCo Python · MuJoCo dynamics and reproducibility · PX4 failure-injection support. All viewer data is embedded; no external scripts or network requests.
